newsitem.title: FRANCE: Scor shares helped by M&G takeover news.
newsitem.headline: Scor shares helped by M&G takeover news.

text.p: Shares in French reinsurance group Scor rose on Tuesday on the back of news that British insurer Prudential Corp had sold its Mercantile & General reinsurance business to Swiss Re, traders said.
Scor shares were up 7.2 francs, or 3.89 percent, at 205.5 francs at 1337 GMT against an overall weaker stock market.
Dealers said the shake-up in the insurance sector with the M&G sale was fuelling speculation over the holdings in Scor.

The French reinsurer is owned to the tune of 40.9 percent by insurer UAP, which said in June that it could reduce its stake when the reinsurer was quoted on the New York stock exchange, due to happen this autumn.
Other Scor shareholders include recently privatised insurer AGF with less than five percent, Axa with seven percent, insurance mutuals with about 10 percent in total and Swiss Life with 2.25 percent.
Prudential sold M&G for 1.75 billion pounds to Swiss Re, which had sold M&G to Prudential nearly 30 years ago.
